title: States Weekly: November 4, 2026
gist: CSIS's weekly digest of Indian state policy: Tamil Nadu's BESS policy targets 2.5 GW/10 GWh storage in three years, Delhi eases C&I renewable open access, Bihar adopts MSME and AI policies, Karnataka plans a $52.66bn urbanization push to decentralize from Bengaluru, and states expand fiscal transfers and DA hikes.

themes.theme: Indian state energy and storage policy

insights.claim: Tamil Nadu's new Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Policy targets deployment of at least 2.5 GW or 10 GWh of energy storage over the next three years, covering both standalone and renewables-co-located storage.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A concrete state-level BESS demand pipeline—relevant to battery suppliers, integrators, and Indian storage developers.
insights.quote: at least 2.5 GW or 10 GWh of energy storage capacity over the next three years

insights.claim: The Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission amended green energy open access rules so commercial and industrial consumers no longer need an 11 kV or higher connection to procure renewable energy via open access.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Widens the addressable market for C&I renewable power sales in Delhi to smaller consumers.
insights.quote: consumers will no longer be required to be connected at 11 kV or above

insights.claim: Haryana suspended implementation of a 25-year electricity distribution license granted to Eleven Power (EEPL) covering Gurugram and Nuh.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Signals regulatory risk for private entrants into Indian power distribution.

insights.claim: Maharashtra waived the 25% transfer fee on land acquired for renewable energy projects when land moves from a parent company to its subsidiary.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Lowers cost of SPV structuring for renewable developers in Maharashtra.

insights.claim: Bihar's MSME Policy 2026 aims to create 10 million direct and indirect jobs over five years, raise the state's credit-deposit ratio to 75%, and set up an MSME cluster and center in each of its 38 districts.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A credit-deposit target of 75% implies a push for more bank lending in a historically under-credited state.
insights.quote: raise the state’s credit-deposit ratio to 75 percent

insights.claim: Bihar approved the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 to make the state an attractive destination for AI companies, startups, and digital enterprises.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Shows AI industrial policy spreading to lower-income Indian states, though without stated incentive figures.

insights.claim: Goa approved the Chief Minister's MSME Innovation Scheme 2026, extending Start-Up Policy incentives to registered MSMEs, and new pollution control rules with fee concessions and simplified online consent for MSMEs.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Incremental ease-of-business measures for small firms.

insights.claim: Karnataka's 20-year State Regional Urbanization Plan 2047 envisages 50+ initiatives across seven pillars with estimated investment of $52.66 billion (INR 5 lakh crore), aiming to reduce dependence on Bengaluru as the primary growth center.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Large long-dated infrastructure ambition; signals policy push toward secondary cities in Karnataka.
insights.quote: reducing dependence on Bengaluru as the primary growth center

insights.claim: Maharashtra amended its PPP Policy 2026 to simplify infrastructure project approvals, reduce administrative delays, and improve interdepartmental coordination.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Could accelerate PPP infrastructure awards in India's largest state economy.

insights.claim: Tamil Nadu let local bodies approve residential buildings up to 1,500 square meters FSI and raised the maximum height for specified non-high-rise buildings from 60 to 64 feet, easing parking rules and expanding developments allowed in Chennai's restricted aquifer recharge area.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Deregulatory moves supportive of Tamil Nadu real estate development activity.
insights.locator: Tamil Nadu amends the Tamil Nadu

insights.claim: Maharashtra approved $789.9 million (INR 7,500 crore) in pre-Diwali drought aid, with about 15 million farmers in 304 drought-hit areas each receiving an advance of INR 5,000.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Adds to state fiscal pressure while supporting rural consumption in the festive season.

insights.claim: Several Indian states raised Dearness Allowance for employees and pensioners: Tamil Nadu by 3%, and Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh by 2% each.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Recurring state wage-bill increases constrain capex room in state budgets.

insights.claim: Haryana broadened its Chirayu-Ayushman Haryana Healthcare Scheme to include middle-income families earning more than $3,100 (INR 3 lakh) annually.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Expanding state health coverage widens the patient base for insured private healthcare.
